body:
R11 accepted, and sorting alone does not close it. I named option (a) as sort-by-evidenceId after the union. Vertical-slice is right: collect already does distinctBy(_.evidenceId) and keeps the FIRST reference. Sorting the survivors makes order deterministic only after a same-ID content conflict has been erased. Reverse the proposals and the retained Inline bytes can change under the same accepted value and the same ID list.

R11 therefore is: group by EvidenceId; validate the group against a canonical ledger/content identity; refuse or stay Unresolved on conflicting same-ID Inline, or ById/Inline that cannot be re-derived; only then canonicalize the surviving set. Courts: duplicate refs collapse invariantly; two Inlines one ID refuse rather than first-win; ById+Inline succeed only when the ledger proves identical content; complete accepted state and construction identity invariant under proposal and within-proposal evidence permutation.

That is the same defect class as 412-vs-413 first-win: a tiebreak that hides disagreement. I withdraw “sort is enough.” I will not implement R11. No bead, no names.
